increments.title: Incoming attack telegraph state
increments.note: Validated attacks carry windup, damage, guard damage, and blockability; expiry resolves exactly one hit. No renderer or enemy-AI cue is claimed.

increments.title: Guard integrity and guard break
increments.note: Ordinary guard spends bounded guard integrity instead of health; an over-limit block breaks guard and applies the attack once.

increments.title: Perfect guard
increments.note: Guard inside the perfect window preserves health and guard integrity and grants one bounded defense counter.

increments.title: Timed dodge and perfect dodge
increments.note: Too-early dodge preserves the threat, normal evade prevents damage, and perfect dodge grants one bounded counter.

increments.title: Defense-earned Fatal Strike counter
increments.note: A valid perfect defense can reduce one eligible Fatal Strike to 35 resource; rejection does not consume the counter and successful use consumes it once.

increments.title: Forgiving perfect-defense timing preset
increments.note: Standard remains default at 0.12 s; optional forgiving preset uses 0.20 s without altering damage, resource, enemy timing, or dodge reach.

community_source.request: A way to make the satisfying but very tight Perfect Guard timing more lenient.
community_source.evidence_limit: Historical discussion, not consensus and not proof the current game retains the same timing. A separate 2024-02-03 thread contains both criticism of strict/reward-light early Perfect Guard and counterexamples describing useful endgame Perfect Guard builds.

verification.repository_regression_tests: exact 8.06/7.94/794x0.01, fractional 60fps, ordinary 122x60Hz deadline, and saturated-clock rebase regressions committed

review_findings.finding: Repeated float subtraction could move an 8.06 s threat across the 0.12 s perfect-defense boundary differently for one 7.94 s step versus 794 x 0.01 s steps.
review_findings.resolution: Replaced remaining-time subtraction with an accumulated defense timeline and integer-microsecond deadlines. Added the exact 8.06/7.94/0.01 boundary and expiry regressions.

review_findings.finding: Quantizing each frame delta independently still allowed fractional-microsecond rounding to diverge between one step and 60 split steps.
review_findings.resolution: Quantize only the accumulated absolute clock at comparison points and retain the direct fractional 60 Hz guard/expiry regressions.

review_findings.finding: A 122-frame 60 Hz sequence could finish one microsecond before the equivalent one-step boundary because the caller supplies rounded float durations.
review_findings.resolution: Added a 100-microsecond canonical comparison tolerance, applied consistently to attack expiry, counter expiry, dodge/perfect windows, and remaining-time queries. Added the exact 122 x 1/60 regression.

review_findings.finding: After a very large finite AdvanceTime saturated the defense clock, newly queued deadlines also saturated and could become instantaneous or unusable.
review_findings.resolution: Before scheduling a threat that cannot fit in the remaining int64 timeline, rebase the idle defense clock while preserving any representable counter remainder. Counter deadlines also rebase if needed. Added a 1e13-second saturation regression verifying a fresh one-second threat remains ordinary at time zero and expires once after one second.
